---
title: "Vector Spaces"
---

::: {#exr-double-negation name="Double additive inverse" .lean-paired lean-id="exr-double-negation"}
Prove that $-(-v)=v$ for every $v\in V$.

#### Solution

Let $v\in V$. By definition, $-v$ is an additive inverse of $v$, so

$$
v+(-v)=0.
$$

Commutativity gives $(-v)+v=0$. But $-(-v)$ is also defined by

$$
(-v)+(-(-v))=0.
$$

Because additive inverses are unique, $-(-v)=v$.
:::

The statement of @exr-double-negation only uses the additive-group structure; no scalar multiplication is needed.
